newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Common position struck on consumer credit directive.
newsitem.headline: Common position struck on consumer credit directive.

text.p: Financial institutions in the European Union will have to apply a common formula for calculating the cost of consumer credit under an agreement reached by the EU's Consumer Affairs Council on Thursday.

Under the common position struck by the Council on the proposal amending directive 87/102/EEC, the so-called consumer credit directive, all the institutions will have to use a common mathematical formula laid down by the EU for calculating the annual percentage rate of charge.
They will have to apply the directive two years after it is formally adopted.
The change has been necessary as differences between the member states have made it difficult for EU consumers to work out who is offering the best deal.
